semantics.note: A hyperbolic general description ('forever', 'endlessly', 'never disclose') of how the industry behaves. It sets no horizon or measure, and an open-ended 'endlessly' cannot be tested.

contract.note: Treating the general phrase 'never disclose' as an absolute rule, refuted by any single disclosure, stretches the words against the speaker. The contract itself admits the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's postmortem discloses that it reverted its own harmful Claude Code prompt. That is one company disclosing one regression rollback, not proof against the general claim, and it does not touch the endless-cycle claim.

reviews.rationale: This is open-ended rhetorical framing, not a scorable forecast. 'Endlessly' can never be confirmed, and a strict reading of 'never disclose' is unfair to a general statement. The single Anthropic rollback disclosure is context and does not decide the claim.

semantics.note: A faithful summary of a past event, the January 3 Perplexity exchange.

contract.note: Reading 'blamed the user' as saying the user's premise came from misinformation is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Wired's firsthand test shows Perplexity denying the capture and blaming 'misinformation'. Perplexity also said the query was sent to a lower-tier model. In the same session Claude found the morning's news.
CNN at 05:20 ET on January 3 reported Trump's announcement of the capture, so reputable reporting existed that morning.
The official record (published January 5) confirms the capture, so the earlier reporting was accurate.

reviews.rationale: Wired documents Perplexity denying the capture and pointing to misinformation. CNN shows credible reporting by early morning, and official records confirm the event. The exact query minute is missing, but the same morning session found the news through Claude, so the order of events is reasonably established.

semantics.note: 'As if either side had any chance' is a firm, sarcastic rejection of complete dominance with no deadline. The drafter's modality 'unlikely' understates how firm the words are, but the proposition itself is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'complete dominance' as sustained, broad superiority in both capability and adoption is ordinary. The resolution rules are fair.

evidence.note: BCG (2026) finds Chinese models keeping pace with US leaders. No dominance yet, but that cannot settle an open-ended exclusion.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet shows no complete dominance by either country, so the early-refutation rule is not met. Continued competition over a finite period cannot confirm that dominance will never happen, so the claim stays unresolved.
